title: Monday, November 9: two dead in Ravine Park, Lake Elmo street assessments, a county trail grant, and a capital plan hearing

script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union for Monday, November 9. Here is the week's news.

Cottage Grove police and the Washington County Sheriff’s Office responded about 6:11 a.m. on November 4 to a report of shots fired in Ravine Park. Officers found two people with gunshot wounds. Both were pronounced dead at the scene. The preliminary investigation indicates the two were known to each other and that the shooting was not a random act of violence. There is no active threat to the community. Ravine Park remains closed until further notice.

Lake Elmo's council meets Wednesday night on tearing down the old elementary school and ordering a street and utility project that would assess $9,800 against each of 89 neighborhood units. Stillwater Area Schools owns the site at 11030 Stillwater Boulevard North. The proposal is for grading and demolition of the existing Lake Elmo Elementary School. The work would disturb about 8.2 acres and requires 41 replacement trees. The same night the council is asked to order the 2027 Street and Utility Improvements in the Oace Acres Neighborhood, covering 1.9 miles. The total estimated cost is $2,897,000. Special assessments would cover $872,200, or $9,800 per unit for 89 units. The regular meeting is at 7 p.m. at City Hall, 3880 Laverne Avenue North.

Washington County commissioners meet Tuesday on a $1,244,000 Environment and Natural Resources Trust Fund grant for the Hardwood Creek Regional Trail Extension. The board would act as state aid sponsor for 2026 Local Road Improvement Program applications that include a 2.7-mile rehabilitation of 30th Street North in West Lakeland Township, a 1.6-mile rehabilitation of Stonebridge Trail North in Stillwater Township, and a 1.1-mile rehabilitation of McKusick Road North in the City of Grant. A workshop follows on the 2027 Proposed Fee Schedule. Black-and-white photocopies would rise from 10 cents to 15 cents a page. Color photocopies would drop from 70 cents to 50 cents. The regular meeting starts at approximately 10:00 a.m. The agenda does not print a meeting place.

Lake Elmo's Planning Commission holds a public hearing Monday, November 9, on the city's 2027–2036 Capital Improvement Plan. The hearing is at 6:30 p.m. at Lake Elmo City Hall, 3880 Laverne Avenue North.

Times and documents are in the show notes.
